source.title: Perplexity-Aware Data Scaling Law: Perplexity Landscapes Predict Performance for Continual Pre-training
source.authors: Lei Liu; Hao Zhu; Xiao-Yan Yang; Yue Shen; Zhi-Xuan Chu; Jian Wang; Jin-Jie Gu; Kui Ren

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a perplexity-based scaling relationship during continual pre-training, a different training regime and formulation from the original parameter/data/compute scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper fits and validates a test-loss relationship using perplexity statistics and reports loss across model-size and compute plots. Benchmark scores and CPT loss-curve comparisons for DOS, random sampling, and low-/high-perplexity sampling are not rows because they evaluate the data-selection method, not whether the scaling relationship holds.
record.test_reason: The core law relates continual pre-training (CPT) test loss to perplexity mean and variance at fixed D=40B, which no version names. Only Figure 3 (loss vs parameters, 0.6B–14B Qwen3) and Figure 2(b) (loss vs FLOPs) bear on scale scaling. Both are in a CPT regime and are figure-only, so they bear on V5, not on V1 pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also claim the selection reaches better adaptation with significantly less data than conventional CPT. They frame the law as moving beyond volume-only scaling laws, which they say yield diminishing returns in CPT.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a fitted law based on perplexity-distribution statistics and CPT test loss, rather than the original laws' parameter, token, and compute scaling setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported loss relationship varies with PPL mean and variance; the authors say their effects are not strictly monotonic and introduce an interaction term. Figure 3 text also says the effect of model size depends on data characteristics.

fits_no_version.finding: CPT test loss depends non-monotonically on the mean and variance of the base model's perplexity over the training subset, with an interior optimum. A multiplicative power-law form with interaction terms fits held-out subsets for Qwen3-0.6B and 14B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In continual pre-training at fixed data size, test loss is predictable from perplexity-distribution statistics of the training data.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The key fitted and validation results are presented in figures without numerical point values or reported fit exponents and uncertainty estimates. Validation uses sampled subsets from the same underlying data distribution and is reported for two Qwen3 model sizes in the medical CPT setting.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 benchmark scores and Figure 6 CPT loss curves compare data-selection strategies and do not directly test the scaling relationship. No other results bearing directly on the tested versions were left out.

untested.parts: No from-scratch pretraining. No token sweep. No power-law fit in N, D or compute.
No extrapolation to larger runs. The validation points come from the same distribution and the same model sizes.
Power-law form in N, D or compute during CPT is not fitted. No other modalities and no repeated data.
Downstream benchmarks are compared only across data-selection methods, not against scale or loss.

missing.what: The paper asserts that marginal gains from more data diminish rapidly in CPT, but shows no data-size sweep supporting this.

record.verdict_notes: No fit parameters, exponents, or numerical losses are reported. The 'generalization' validation is interpolation within the same distribution and model sizes. The FLOPs and parameter plots are unexplained beyond qualitative statements. The record listed ACL as the peer-review venue, but the source text does not show this.

versions.untested_parts: No reported token-count sweep; the parameter and compute plots do not establish a power-law fit in those quantities.
No extrapolation from small runs to runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or comparison of optimal parameter and token growth.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests a perplexity-aware law in medical continual pre-training; does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer settings beyond CPT.
No test of downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Does not test dependence of classic law exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup or fitting choices, or disagreement between published laws.

rows.subject: Qwen3-14B-Base
rows.operation_detail: Fits a test-loss scaling relationship using perplexity-distribution statistics from sampled PubMed subsets.

conditions.value: PPL mean and variance; plotted fit points and curves

rows.measure: Test loss as a function of PPL distribution statistics
rows.note: The authors state that loss versus mean or variance is not strictly monotonic and introduce an interaction term; the simpler monotonic formulation does not capture the reported relationship. The fitted formulation retains a power-law structure.
rows.check: Loss vs PPL mean/variance at fixed data size is a data-quality relationship, not scaling in parameters, tokens or compute. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Qwen3-14B-Base
rows.note: The figure plots log test loss against FLOPs, but the text does not describe the curve's shape or report fit parameters.
rows.check: This is CPT loss, not from-scratch pretraining loss, so it bears on V5 rather than V1. The text never describes the FLOPs curve's shape or fit.

rows.subject: Qwen3 models shown in Figure 3(a)
rows.size_stated: 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B, and 14B are shown in the figure
rows.operation_detail: Plots test loss across parameter counts under a low-PPL setting.

conditions.value: low; plotted settings include σ values shown in Figure 3(a)

rows.note: The authors state that loss decreases with model size, but the text does not establish a power-law fit for this sweep or assign numeric losses to individual parameter counts.
rows.check: This is CPT loss, not pretraining, so V5 rather than V1. The text says loss decreases with N, but no power-law fit is reported and the size range is only 0.6B–14B. Partial: monotone decrease without an established power law.

rows.subject: Qwen3 models shown in Figure 3(b)
rows.size_stated: 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B, and 14B are shown in the figure
rows.operation_detail: Plots test loss across parameter counts under a high-PPL setting.

conditions.value: high; plotted settings include σ values shown in Figure 3(b)

rows.note: The authors state that loss decreases with model size and that the magnitude depends on data characteristics; the text does not establish a power-law fit for this sweep.
rows.check: This is CPT, so V5 rather than V1. In the high-PPL range, the text says higher σ 'limits' scaling with N. No power-law fit is reported.

rows.subject: Qwen3-0.6B-Base
rows.operation_detail: Evaluates held-out validation points against the fitted loss relationship as PPL variance varies.

conditions.value: 10% of sampled subsets; different PPL profiles from the fitting subsets

rows.measure: Test loss versus PPL variance; validation against fitted scaling-law region
rows.value: figure only; text says validation points closely follow the predicted trend and remain largely within the region
rows.note: The authors report small, symmetric deviations without systematic bias; numeric point values are not supplied in the text.
rows.check: This validates the loss-vs-PPL-variance law, not a scale law. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Qwen3-14B-Base
rows.operation_detail: Evaluates held-out validation points against the fitted loss relationship as PPL variance varies.

conditions.value: 10% of sampled subsets; different PPL profiles from the fitting subsets

rows.measure: Test loss versus PPL variance; validation against fitted scaling-law region
rows.value: figure only; text says validation points closely follow the predicted trend and remain largely within the region
rows.note: The authors report small, symmetric deviations without systematic bias; numeric point values are not supplied in the text.
rows.check: This validates the loss-vs-PPL-variance law, not a scale law. Moved to fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: Qwen3 0.6B–14B continual pre-training on PubMed, low- and high-PPL data subsets (Figure 3)
relationships.reason: Loss falls with model size, but no power law is fitted. The text says the magnitude depends on PPL variance, with high σ limiting scaling in the high-PPL range (r3, r4).
relationships.display_finding: Loss decreased with model size, but gain magnitude depended on perplexity variance, with high variance weakening scaling among high-perplexity subsets.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen3-0.6B-Base and Qwen3-14B-Base validation points on sampled PubMed subsets
reader_labels.reason: Both models' validation losses are reported to closely follow the fitted PPL-variance trend, with small, symmetric deviations and no systematic bias (r5, r6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Relationship between test loss and PPL mean/variance in the fitted formulation
reader_labels.reason: The authors report non-monotonic relationships with the individual PPL statistics and add an interaction term; the simpler monotonic formulation is insufficient (r1).
